name: agent-companion
description: Guardrails and calibration for agent teams: keeps the main thread delegating, caps premium-model fan-out, holds agents to a short reporting contract, watches instruction budget, backs up the memory corpus, and detects harness drift.

delegation_guard.title: Delegation guard
delegation_guard.description: Nudge the MAIN thread to delegate after repeated execution-class tool calls. Never applies inside subagents.

delegation_threshold.title: Delegation threshold
delegation_threshold.description: Consecutive main-thread execution calls tolerated before the guard fires.

premium_cap.title: Premium fan-out cap
premium_cap.description: Limit how many premium-tier (fable/opus) subagents may run concurrently.

premium_max_concurrent.title: Max concurrent premium agents
premium_max_concurrent.description: How many premium-tier subagents may run at once before further spawns are denied.

warrant_required.title: Premium warrant
warrant_required.description: Require a stated justification when spawning a premium-tier subagent.

memory_budget.title: Memory budget monitor
memory_budget.description: Warn when always-loaded instruction files get too large, and write a refactor prompt.

memory_budget_tokens.title: Memory budget (tokens)
memory_budget_tokens.description: Token ceiling for a single always-loaded instruction file before it is flagged.

spawn_telemetry.title: Spawn telemetry
spawn_telemetry.description: Record every subagent spawn (model, type, agent_type) for the calibration routine.

memory_doctor.title: Memory doctor
memory_doctor.description: Detect unreachable memory files (on disk but absent from the index) and broken index links. Repair is non-destructive and opt-in via --fix.

memory_archive_prefixes.title: Historical memory prefixes
memory_archive_prefixes.description: Comma-separated filename prefixes treated as historical and safe to archive. Anything else is treated as a live rule and re-linked instead.

memory_vault.title: Memory vault backup
memory_vault.description: Keep a local git history of the memory corpus (~/.claude/projects/*/memory/) in a separate repository under ~/.claude/agent-companion/memory-vault/, so a rewrite or truncation is no longer unrecoverable. Strictly read-only against the live corpus — it is a mirrored copy, never a git working tree of the corpus itself (see docs/adr/0001-memory-corpus-backup-vault.md). DEFAULT OFF, like memory_search/memory_brief, because this plugin is distributed publicly and turning this on writes a second, permanent, versioned copy of someone's personal memory to disk. `sync()` checks this option as its first line, so a hand run of `node scripts/memory-vault.mjs sync` with the option off is a no-op — set this option, or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_MEMORY_VAULT, to actually sync. Stricter than memory-doctor.mjs and memory-search.mjs, which do not gate their CLI path on a master option at all.

telemetry_endpoint.title: Telemetry endpoint
telemetry_endpoint.description: Optional. Full URL to POST emitted telemetry to at session end. EMPTY BY DEFAULT — while empty the plugin makes no network calls at all. Setting it is the only thing that turns sending on.

telemetry_tenant.title: Telemetry tenant
telemetry_tenant.description: Tenant key sent with uploads when a telemetry endpoint is configured.

telemetry_interval_cloud_min.title: Cloud send interval (minutes)
telemetry_interval_cloud_min.description: How often a cloud session ships telemetry at turn boundaries. Cloud filesystems vanish with the session and there is no later sweep, so this is shorter than the local interval.

telemetry_interval_local_min.title: Local send interval (minutes)
telemetry_interval_local_min.description: How often a local session ships telemetry at turn boundaries. Local runs are backstopped by the on-disk JSONL, so this can be relaxed.

scout_surface.title: Scout surface
scout_surface.description: At session start, surface unresolved signals from the last locally scheduled scout run. Silent when the scout found nothing.

fit_guard.title: Best-fit guard
fit_guard.description: When a spawn brief declares WEIGHT (and optionally KIND / CONSEQUENCE), grade the named model against the routing table: under- and cheap-over-provisioned spawns are allowed and announced; a premium model over-provisioned for its own declared weight is denied with the correction. Off = telemetry only.

fit_autofill.title: Best-fit autofill
fit_autofill.description: When a spawn declares WEIGHT but names no model, set the model from the routing table instead of letting it inherit the lead’s tier. Premium results still require a WARRANT line.

foreground_guard.title: Foreground-spawn guard
foreground_guard.description: How to treat a MAIN-SESSION spawn that is not run_in_background: true. A foreground spawn blocks the lead's entire turn until it returns — measured baseline: most main-session spawns run foreground, and individual foreground spawns have locked the operator out for 18-27 minutes, unable to act on messages sent mid-turn. "off": nothing. "warn" (default): a systemMessage naming the cost and the fix, zero model tokens. "block": deny unless the brief states a line of the form `FOREGROUND: <why>`, escapable exactly like the premium warrant. Either way, a spawn whose resolved model is the plugin's own cheapest known tier (haiku) is exempt — cheapest is also fastest, so blocking the lead's turn for one is genuinely low-cost; an unknown or unresolved model is never exempt. This is NOT Anthropic guidance — Claude Code publishes no foreground-vs-background recommendation, so this default is this plugin's own operating decision.

isolation_demotion_notice.title: Isolation demotion notice
isolation_demotion_notice.description: Tell the caller when a spawn passes BOTH name and isolation: per agent-teams.md, passing isolation on the call makes it an ordinary subagent rather than a teammate even though it is named, so it silently will not be addressable by that name afterward. Pure information, never blocks, effectively free to compute.

shared_tree_notice.title: Shared-tree spawn notice
shared_tree_notice.description: Tell the caller when a spawn has NEITHER a name NOR isolation: it runs in the lead's own working tree (can commit there, moving HEAD) and has no address to re-brief it later — the worst-of-both-worlds shape. Deliberately narrow (unnamed AND unisolated only, not every unisolated spawn — most unisolated spawns are harmless reads) so the notice stays rare enough to read rather than becoming background noise.

version_notice.title: Version divergence notice
version_notice.description: Tell the user, once per session per (plugin, lastUpdated) pair, when ANY installed plugin — not just this one — was updated after this session last loaded its plugins (session start, or the last /reload-plugins). Also keeps this plugin's own running-vs-installed self-check, the one thing that catches a desktop session that loaded a stale app-extracted bundle at startup; the two are merged into a single notice when both fire. Fires at session start and again on the next prompt, so a stale mid-session update is caught, not just a stale startup. Read-only and user-facing only (never added to model context, zero tokens); default ON because it is the one thing that prevents a session and every sub-agent it spawns from silently running stale hooks and skills for hours.

memory_search.title: Memory search
memory_search.description: Master switch for BM25 retrieval over the operator's memory corpus. Gates the spawn-time memory brief below (memory_brief also has to be on). Does not gate scripts/memory-search.mjs itself — like memory-doctor.mjs, that CLI runs whenever invoked directly; this only controls automatic use from a hook. Read-only with respect to memory files; the index it builds is derived and disposable.

memory_brief.title: Memory brief at spawn
memory_brief.description: Master switch for saying something about the memory corpus in a subagent's brief at spawn time. WHICH behaviour runs is chosen by memory_brief_mode. Requires memory_search to also be on (that is the outer master switch).

memory_brief_mode.title: Memory brief mode
memory_brief_mode.description: Which spawn-time memory behaviour runs when memory_brief is on. "nudge" (default): threshold-free and relevance-blind — appends one short line saying a searchable memory corpus exists, how many files this project has, how many other projects have one, and the exact search command; never scores or ranks content, so it cannot be wrong the way a score-gated block can. "pointers": the original BM25-ranked block, gated by memory_brief_max_hits/memory_brief_min_score (see that key's description for why an absolute score threshold cannot separate relevance from brief length on this operator's corpus — pointers mode is not the default because of that finding). "off": memory_brief is on but neither behaviour runs.

memory_brief_max_hits.title: Memory brief max hits (pointers mode only)
memory_brief_max_hits.description: How many memory pointers to append to a spawn brief at most. Applies only when memory_brief_mode is "pointers"; nudge mode ignores this.

memory_brief_min_score.title: Memory brief minimum score (pointers mode only)
memory_brief_min_score.description: Applies only when memory_brief_mode is "pointers"; nudge mode ignores this and uses no score at all. Raw BM25 score (k1=1.2, b=0.75, summed over matched query terms) the top hit must clear before any pointer block is appended. Below this the brief is left untouched. Calibrated against this operator's real corpus: a genuinely on-topic long brief scored 21.63, an off-topic-but-plausible long brief scored 17.65, a nonsense long brief scored 6.71, and a genuinely on-topic SHORT brief scored only 10.70 — below the off-topic long case. BM25 sums over query terms, so score tracks brief length almost as much as relevance; no fixed threshold separates the two on this corpus (25 sits above the on-topic long case itself), and relative gating (top/median ratio) is worse — the nonsense query produced the highest ratio measured (1.33). This is why memory_brief_mode defaults to "nudge" instead of tuning this number further.

memory_search_repo.title: Memory search repo scope
memory_search_repo.description: Also index the checked-out repository itself (walking up from cwd to the nearest .git) alongside the operator's user-scope memory corpus. This is the ONLY scope available in a cloud session, where ~/.claude/projects does not exist. A repo root that is itself a git worktree is indexed as its own in-flight branch content; its own .claude/worktrees/** (sibling checkouts of OTHER branches) is always excluded so they are never duplicated into the same index.

memory_search_repo_globs.title: Repo scope globs
memory_search_repo_globs.description: Comma-separated glob list, resolved against the repo root. A hardcoded .claude/** glob finds files in some repos and nothing in others (repos vary in whether they keep a .claude/ directory at all), so this is configurable rather than assumed.

memory_search_max_file_kb.title: Repo scope max file size (KB)
memory_search_max_file_kb.description: Skip any repo-scope file larger than this before indexing it. Skipped files are counted, not silently dropped — --stats reports how many.

memory_search_max_repo_mb.title: Repo scope max total size (MB)
memory_search_max_repo_mb.description: Cap on total bytes indexed from the repo scope across all matched files. A docs/ tree alone can reach several MB on a large repo, so this cap is mandatory rather than advisory: once reached, further files stop being added and the index is marked partial/truncated so a caller can say so instead of silently under-reporting.

coverage_partial_ratio.title: Telemetry coverage partial-day ratio
coverage_partial_ratio.description: A day is flagged 'partial' (not fully silent, but under-recorded) when spawns.jsonl has fewer than this fraction of that day's real Agent tool_use calls seen in transcripts. Used by the telemetry-coverage audit check and the enforcement_silent scout signal.

brevity.title: Reporting contract
brevity.description: Append a short reporting contract to every spawned agent’s brief: status line, blockers in full, outcome as facts, no progress narration. This is the global default — `brevity off` at the CLI overrides it at runtime, and a per-agent entry overrides both, in either direction.

brevity_peer.title: Peer brevity (always)
brevity_peer.description: Agent-to-agent messages are a decision or a fact, one screen at most. Deliberately SEPARATE from the reporting contract: turning the contract off for an agent still leaves this clause in place, because succinctness between agents was asked for unconditionally.

brevity_reinforce.title: Reporting contract self-heal
brevity_reinforce.description: At SubagentStart, re-inject the contract as context ONLY when it is absent from the prompt the subagent actually received — i.e. when the spawn-time rewrite did not take (another hook’s updatedInput won, or a stale plugin copy ran). Never double-injects.

brevity_telemetry.title: Report-length telemetry
brevity_telemetry.description: Record each subagent’s final-report length, agent type, and whether the contract was on, to telemetry/brevity.jsonl. This is what makes the feature auditable rather than merely believed: which agent types are actually verbose, and whether the contract moved the number.

brevity_stop_gate.title: Over-long report gate (experimental)
brevity_stop_gate.description: Block a final report longer than brevity_report_max_chars ONCE per agent and ask for it again in the contract shape. Off by default because a SubagentStop block feeds the reason back to the same subagent, costing it a full extra turn — it only pays off where reports are routinely enormous. Capped at one block per agent so it can never loop.

brevity_report_max_chars.title: Over-long report threshold (characters)
brevity_report_max_chars.description: Final-report length above which brevity_stop_gate fires. Ignored while that gate is off.

standing_rules.title: Standing rules
standing_rules.description: Operator-authored “always do X if Y” rules, injected at session start, on matching prompts, and into matching spawn briefs. Conditions are a regex over the text (`when`) plus an optional session-state gate. Edit with scripts/rules.mjs; five rules ship built in.

standing_rules_max_chars.title: Standing rules budget (characters)
standing_rules_max_chars.description: Ceiling on the rendered rule block per injection. Rules past the ceiling are dropped and the count is stated, so a budget overrun is visible rather than silent.

publication_leak_sweep.title: Publication-leak sweep enabled
publication_leak_sweep.description: Master switch. OFF by default: this feature clones/fetches repos and, locally, calls the GitHub API (via `gh` if installed) to auto-discover which ones — real network and process activity a public plugin should not perform until an operator opts in. When on, LOCAL auto-discovers every public repo you can push to (owned + org-member, via `gh`) PLUS any local checkout under your dev root whose origin is a public GitHub repo, unions and dedupes them, and sweeps all of them daily. Use `publication_leak_repos` to add repos discovery would miss or exclude ones it shouldn't cover. See "Publication-leak sweep" in the setup skill before turning this on.

publication_leak_repos.title: Publication-leak sweep: extra / excluded repos
publication_leak_repos.description: Only consulted when publication_leak_sweep is on. Comma-separated. A plain entry (a local checkout path, `owner/repo`, or a full git URL) is ADDED to auto-discovery — never filtered, so this is also how to cover a fork or archived repo discovery skips on purpose. A `!`-prefixed entry (`!owner/repo`, `!<url>`, or `!<local path>`) is EXCLUDED from whatever discovery found. Leave empty to sweep exactly what auto-discovery finds. LOCAL: each covered repo's origin default branch is fetched into a throwaway clone and scanned by the PLUGIN's own generic checker (derived names, private paths — always) plus that repo's own scripts/leak-check.mjs when it has one (most won't; that's normal, not an error). CLOUD: never clones (the sandbox's classifier denies clone-then-execute) — it scans, in place and --no-derived, only the ONE covered repo that IS the cloud session's own checkout, after confirming HEAD matches origin's default branch; any other covered repo is skipped there, not fetched. Fires publication_leak only for hits not already accepted in a prior run, and publication_repo_newly_public the first time a covered repo is seen as public — the highest-risk moment, so that one is never deduped away.
